title: Desk note: weekly update
bottom_line: Gold ended the fortnight where it started: 3,886, -0.3% since the last weekly forecast on 30 Oct, after a round trip to 4,114 on 9 Nov. The first week ran on oil, which fell on US-Iran diplomacy; the second on rates, as strong payrolls and hot CPI and PPI lifted the 10-year yield to 5.15% and the dollar to its highest close of 2026, and Thursday's 3,885 was the lowest close of the year. The close sits at the 47th percentile of the 30 Oct forecast, inside its 90% range, and inside the ranges of the 2 Nov and 12 Nov notes. Model volatility is up to 23.5% from 21.3%: the model gives a 62% chance of trading below $3,800 within a month and 55% of trading back above $4,000; the two overlap, because one path can do both. Next: Warsh on Monday, retail sales on Tuesday and the FOMC minutes on Wednesday.

bullets.title: Two weeks, two drivers
bullets.text: in the first week gold traded opposite to oil, as it did in October: crude fell on US-Iran diplomacy and gold rallied to 4,114. In the second week the driver switched to rates: the 10-year yield rose from 4.86% to 5.15% and the dollar index from 102.3 to 103.4 while oil kept falling, and gold gave the whole rally back.

bullets.title: Data revived the hike story
bullets.text: October payrolls rose 165,000 against about 65,000 expected; October CPI beat on both headline and core; and PPI rose 6.5% on the year, the most since November 2022 (Kitco). A 25 bp hike at the 8-9 December FOMC is now fully priced, and the odds of 50 bp rose from about 1% before CPI to about 11% (CME FedWatch, per press).

bullets.title: Iran headlines cut both ways
bullets.text: Thursday's drop came as oil rose on Trump's remark that the US no longer wants a deal with Iran (per Panthere Group); by Friday reports said he had eased fears of a renewed war, and oil headed for a second weekly loss (The National). Single-outlet attributions; treat with care.

bullets.title: Demand backdrop
bullets.text: the World Gold Council's Q3 report shows central-bank buying up 42% on the year at 321 tonnes, but it halved its 2026 investment-demand growth forecast to 200 tonnes. ETF flows slowed in October but stayed positive (Money Metals).
